claims.text: Hallucinations in data-to-text generation can be mitigated by combining the probabilistic output of a generator language model with a text critic classifier.
The text critic classifier guides text generation by assessing the match between the input data and the text generated so far.
Critic-driven decoding requires no changes to the underlying language model architecture or training procedure.
Critic-driven decoding can be combined with any model and decoding scheme that operates on word probabilities.
The text critic classifier trains using the base language model's training data and synthetic negative examples without additional training data.

evidence.description: The authors explore combining the probabilistic output of a generator language model with the output of a special text critic classifier to mitigate hallucinations.
The critic classifier guides generation by assessing the match between the input data and the text generated so far.
The method does not need any changes to the underlying LM's architecture or training procedure.
The proposed method can be combined with any model and decoding operating on word probabilities.
The critic does not need any additional training data, using the base LM's training data and synthetic negative examples.

methodologies.name: Critic-Driven Decoding
methodologies.description: A decoding technique combining generator LM output probabilities with a text critic classifier trained on base LM data and synthetic negative examples to evaluate data-text matching.

limitations.text: Existing hallucination mitigation methods typically require altering model architecture or collecting additional data, making them hard to apply to existing models.
